summary: Round-7 verify, scope limited to the rounds:M4.43 cap argument in baselines/review.txt:18 (the three backlog rows and the done-row already carry a pass from me). No code changed, so I ran no build and no mutation; every claim in the delta was checked against .harness/review and against the staged bytes of the four touched files. M4.43-R5a IS FIXED, exactly: 'THE PRODUCTION REVIEWER re-measured independently, recording fast=6, 7, 7 for the 2x mutant at a 2000ms window' is M4.43-R1d verbatim (68c714405ad5...reviewer.json: 'I measured the same configuration in my own tree ... and got fast=6, fast=7, fast=7', 2000ms window, multipliedBy(2)); the disagreement replacing the retraction checks out at e8a3151c, where the test verdict (mtime 05:38:52, TR-M4.17-3) reads 'THE FLOOR OF 4 DOES NOT KILL multipliedBy(2); it kills it about 40% of the time' and the production verdict (mtime 05:40:17) reads 'the raised rate floor kills multipliedBy(2) ... so the floor keeps 1.75x slack', and no verdict anywhere withdraws the second. The uneven-standard clause is right (the twelve-run series was in 57281fcd's draft and no production series of that length exists in .harness; the retraction clause survived one clause away). M0.64 resolves and says what the entry says it says (backlog.md:33 / backlog-notes.md:45, 'A REVIEWER CAN REPORT A VERDICT IT NEVER RECORDED'). The test review's self-retraction is exact: TR-M4.17-6 (3893ebde) proposed 'raise the floor from 3 to 4' off 'green 5/5 ... fastRate=3 slowRate=0 every run', and TR-M4.17-3 (e8a3151c) withdrew it off 'fastRate = 4, 3, 4, 4, 3 over five class-scoped runs ... plus two full :sequencer:test runs'. R5b's ordinal is gone. SWEEP FOR DUPLICATES: grepped 'retract|withdrew|final round|arrived last|7, not 6|1.75|fast=6|fastRate' across all four staged files -- the retraction claim, the round narrative and the 6/7 attribution exist in exactly one copy each, and backlog-notes.md:309 (M4.41) already says 'fastRate=7 ... in one tree and fastRate=6,7,7 in another', which agrees with the new per-role attribution. TWO MINORS, both new in this delta and both the counting/attribution shape this entry is about: the round-relative claim R5b flagged survived its own fix inside the clause that now declares the entry states no round outcome, and the cap argument equates all three filed rows with an error its own done-row says only two of them are. Both land under minors-land; the do-not-split conclusion is unaffected by either and no session is sent to do wrong work.

findings.title: The round-relative claim R5b flagged survived the removal of its ordinal -- inside the clause that now declares the entry states no round outcome -- and both readings of 'the two that arrived last' are contradicted by .harness
findings.detail: The closing sentence now reads '⚠️ THIS ENTRY CLAIMS NO CONVERGENCE, and states no round outcome, because a round fact carried by hand in prose is stale by the round after it -- `rounds:M4.7a` in this file says so ... Findings kept arriving after each fix, and the two that arrived last were introduced by the fix before them and were both the same counting shape. They are recorded in the commit body rather than chased'. The ordinal R5b named ('the final round passed both roles') is gone; the round fact it qualified is not, and the entry does state a round outcome one clause after promising not to. By mtime over .harness/review for task M4.43: 961791a8 (test, changes-requested, TR-1/TR-2); 68c71440 (reviewer, changes-requested, R1a-R1d); 0d447714 (test pass TR-3/4/5, reviewer changes-requested R2a-R2d); b0a1c839 (reviewer pass R3a/R3b, test pass TR-2); 57281fcd (reviewer changes-requested, R4a major); d7b93c2c (reviewer changes-requested R5a major + R5b minor, test changes-requested TR-M4.43-3 major + TR-4 minor). EITHER READING FAILS, which is verbatim the structure R5b used against the predecessor clause. (a) As a claim about R3a/R3b -- the pair that really were two counting-shape minors introduced by the fix to R2a -- 'arrived last' is false: two further rounds and six further findings came after them, two of them majors against this very line. (b) As a claim about the findings that did arrive last (d7b93c2c) it is false three ways: there are four, not two; two are majors (M4.43-R5a, TR-M4.43-3), not minors; and they are not 'the same counting shape' -- R5a/TR-3 are the unsupported retraction attribution and R5b is a stale ordinal, neither of which is a miscount. The next sentence inherits the same referent and adds a claim this delta itself refutes: 'They are recorded in the commit body rather than chased' -- the findings that arrived last were chased, and this delta is the chase. SECOND, IN THE SAME SENTENCE, THE CITED AUTHORITY DOES NOT SAY WHAT IT IS CITED FOR. rounds:M4.7a is four lines up in this same file (baselines/review.txt:13) and reads 'the count is left to `review_rounds.py`, because a count carried by hand in prose is stale by the round after it'. It defers the COUNT and nothing else, and its own body then narrates round outcomes by ordinal -- 'Round 1: `SubscriptionHub` was updated for the KEY and not for the BYTES ... Round 4: passed both roles clean, no findings'. So 'a round fact carried by hand in prose is stale by the round after it -- `rounds:M4.7a` in this file says so' widens the cited rule and attributes to M4.7a a practice M4.7a does not follow. If this is fixed at all rather than recorded (review.md: a minor on a pass is recorded, and this line has now produced findings in three consecutive rounds by being redrafted), the cheap fix is deletion, not another draft: drop 'Findings kept arriving after each fix, and the two that arrived last were introduced by the fix before them and were both the same counting shape', give the surviving 'recorded in the commit body rather than chased' a referent that is not round-relative, and narrow the M4.7a citation to the count.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.15 (M4's VERIFIED.md and milestone review) is the next open row and reads both baselines/review.txt and .harness/review. It reads that the findings which arrived last on M4.43 were two counting-shape minors introduced by the previous fix and recorded rather than chased, and reconstructs the tail of this task as having settled into agreement. .harness shows the opposite: the last round returned two majors -- M4.43-R5a and TR-M4.43-3, both against this exact line, both about a claim the record does not support -- and both were fixed rather than recorded. The auditor either repeats the entry's own account into VERIFIED.md, putting a false round history into the milestone record, or discovers the mismatch and has to re-derive the whole sequence by hand; and the entry that carries it is the one whose stated standard is 'ATTRIBUTED PER ROLE AND ONLY AS THE RECORD SUPPORTS IT', in the permanent file whose entire worth is that its entries are checkable against .harness.

findings.title: 'exactly what the three rows this commit files are about' is contradicted by this commit's own done-row, which says only two of the three are that error -- and the notes rows support only one
findings.detail: The new clause reads 'An under-sampled reading corrected by the same reviewer that took more samples is exactly what the three rows this commit files are about'. The done-row added by this same commit says otherwise, in the sentence written expressly to name rather than count the rows: 'M4.41 and M4.44 are two instances of one error and M4.42 is a second error: a number read from ONE run and reported as a measurement ..., and a false claim corrected in one copy while its duplicate stood.' Two of the three, on the commit's own account, and the notes rows support only one. M4.42 (backlog-notes.md:313) is 'THE CORRECTION WAS APPLIED TO ONE COPY ONLY' plus a third copy standing in production -- a duplicate-survives error with no sampling in it, and its correction was applied by the author to one location, not by a reviewer that took more samples. M4.44 (backlog-notes.md:317) is 'the third distinct comment in this milestone stating a measurement nobody ran' and 'BOTH ROLES MEASURED THAT WRONG, independently' -- zero runs corrected by two different roles, not too few runs corrected by the same one; M4.43-R3b already flagged the attempt to fold M4.44 into the one-run class, and the done-row's 'two instances of one error' is what survived that. Only M4.41 is an under-sampled reading corrected by the same reviewer. A charitable reading ('all three are claims corrected once someone did the work') is available, but 'exactly' and 'the same reviewer' are load-bearing and the done-row denies the equation in the same diff. This is the over-count shape the entry itself files three rows about -- 'the two minors' when four were recorded, 'BOTH ROWS' when three were filed -- applied this time to its own filings.
findings.failure_scenario: A session picks M4.42 off the backlog and reads the cap argument for context, since baselines/review.txt is the only place the three rows are discussed together. It is told all three are under-sampled readings, so it goes looking for a number to re-measure with more runs. M4.42's actual work is finding and deleting the third copy of a false sentence -- LocalSequencer.java's empty-means-fenced branch, 'Another node holds the term now, and it has sealed this chain' -- where no measurement exists to take. The session re-runs LocalSequencerRenewTest, sees green, and closes the row with the production comment still asserting a seal that has not landed, which is exactly the 'one copy fixed while its duplicate stands' outcome M4.42 was filed to prevent and which its own row warns about ('A session that fixes only the test closes this row with the production comment still false').
